records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System

ai_features.name: Auto ElastQ
ai_features.function: Automatically selects up to three stable frames from a 2D shear-wave elastography cineloop and auto-places the measurement ROI in homogeneous, temporally stable regions for liver stiffness measurement (C5-1 transducer). Summary calls it a 'software algorithm' and 'workflow-enhancement software feature'; it does not use the words AI/ML/deep learning.
ai_features.quote: The Auto ElastQ software feature is intended to assist users in making stiffness measurements using 2D-SWE in the liver by recommending specific frames and ROI positions to the user.

records.exclusion_reason: Sole subject of the clearance is Auto ElastQ, a liver 2D shear-wave elastography frame/ROI recommendation feature (retrospective study vs expert manual measurements, 'high agreement', no numbers given). No cardiac AI feature is described.

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System

ai_features.name: AutoMeasure V3 (Auto Measure)
ai_features.function: Semi-automated adult transthoracic echocardiography 2D, Doppler and M-mode measurements generated by an AI detection algorithm trained with machine learning; caliper positions are initialized by the algorithm and the user edits/accepts/rejects. V3 adds M-mode TAPSE, new 2D measurements (LA Vol A2C/A4C, LA diameter PLAX, RA volume, aortic annulus diameter), new Doppler measurements (MR VTI, TR VTI), new detectors, and re-trained existing detectors. Requires ECG and an adult cardiology TTE transducer.
ai_features.quote: Auto Measure is an optional software feature on the EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System that provides the end user with semiautomated adult echocardiography 2D, Doppler or M-mode measurements through an AI-algorithm, training via machine-learning techniques.

records.performance_summary: Retrospective performance validation of AutoMeasure V3 on 7127 TTE cardiac clips from 3964 adult subjects (multi-institution USA/Asia/Europe, enrolled 2015-June 2024; age 59.0+/-16.7 y; 48.6% male; 45.2% Black, 30.3% White, 2.7% Asian, 21.9% other/mixed; BMI 28.9+/-7.1). Ground truth = standard-of-care measurements by qualified healthcare professionals. 32 hypotheses (one per parameter) tested via confidence intervals on Bland-Altman limits of agreement; all met pre-defined acceptance criteria derived from inter-observer variability; stratified analyses by age, BMI, sex, race and clinical status. No per-parameter numeric results are reported in the summary. Quote (p.16): 'The results of the 32 hypotheses tested, demonstrated high agreement of AutoMeasure V3 software with Standard of Care Measurements (ground truth) obtained during initial subject exam, by producing confidence intervals for the limits of agreement, for each parameter (hypothesis) tested, meeting the pre-defined acceptance criteria for the study.'

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System
records.exclusion_reason: Sole subject of the clearance is Remote Software Management (RSM), a remote upgrade/patch deployment feature (OS packages, drivers, BIOS, application packages, scheduled downloads). No AI/ML feature is identifiable in the summary (p.6: 'introduce Remote Software Management (RSM) software feature onto the EPIQ and Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems'). Predicate is K242020 (Auto ElastQ); the AI-list inclusion presumably reflects features carried on the platform rather than anything described here.

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems

ai_features.name: Auto EF with contrast (2D Auto EF Adv / Contrast EF)
ai_features.function: AI-based automated left ventricular ejection fraction from contrast-enhanced adult TTE apical 4-chamber and 2-chamber views, giving single-plane EF for each view and biplane Simpson's EF; manual border edit on ED/ES frames with recalculation. Algorithm previously cleared as LVivo CE-EF (K243235, DiA Imaging Analysis) and integrated unmodified into EPIQ/Affiniti VM13 within the Auto EF Adv application.
ai_features.quote: Auto EF with contrast is an AI based automated software feature that assists clinicians with assessing Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction ( LVEF) from images acquired with contrast agent as part of an adult transthoracic echo (TTE) examination. The feature is located within the Philips Auto EF Adv application.

ai_features.name: Segmental Wall Motion (SWM) v2
ai_features.function: Machine-learning-based automatic evaluation of LV segmental (regional) wall motion from three apical views (A4C, A2C, A3C) with border detection/tracking to produce per-segment wall motion scores and Wall Motion Score Index; user can edit scores. VM13 replaces the SWM version from software v11 with the algorithm cleared under K243862 (LVivo) without modification.
ai_features.quote: The SWM v2 software automatically evaluates the segmental (regional) function of the left ventricle (LV) from adult TTE echo examinations. For input, the SWM algorithm uses 3 apical views (A4C, A2C and A3C) and performs border detection and tracking to identify each of the LV segments based on the three views.

records.performance_summary: Auto EF with contrast: retrospective study on contrast-enhanced TTE clips; ground truth = consensus manual Simpson's biplane EF by 3 sonographers reviewed by an echo cardiologist. Acceptance criterion: lower 95% confidence bound of Pearson r > 0.75. Sub-analysis on Philips-acquired data met the criterion: r = 0.952 (95% CI 0.919, 0.972) for biplane EF (p.12: 'the Pearson's correlation coefficient and associated confidence intervals are 0.952 (95%CI 0.919, 0.972)'). Bland-Altman agreement described as acceptable; sample size not stated. SWM v2: retrospective study on Philips TTE clips comparing automated WMSI to visual estimation by 3 expert cardiologists; sensitivity/specificity analysed against averaged and 2/3-majority ground truths; no numeric values reported, only that performance 'aligns with previously reported assessment of the algorithm (K243862)' (p.12).

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System

ai_features.name: R-Trigger (non-ECG, AI-based R-wave detection)
ai_features.function: AI algorithm that detects the R-wave peak (R-trigger, end-diastole timing) directly from acquired cardiac TTE clips when the ECG physio signal is unavailable or unusable, serving as backup input to AutoStrain LV, AutoEF, 2D Auto LV and AutoMeasure. Works in the background; enables those cardiac applications on clips without ECG. Implemented in VM13.
ai_features.quote: The R-Trigger AI software feature on Philips EPIQ and Affiniti Ultrasound System is intended to support detection of R-wave peak (R-trigger) as an input to AutoStrain and AutoMeasure applications, as well as other cardiac clinical applications.

records.performance_summary: Retrospective validation on 7309 cardiac TTE clips from 3964 subjects acquired on Philips systems (AutoMeasure cohort: age 59.0+/-16.7 y, 48.6% male, 45.2% Black, 30.3% White; R-trigger timestamp cohort n=1894; AutoStrain cohort n=82). 35 hypotheses across 3 endpoints, all met. Endpoint 1 (R-wave timestamp vs ECG): Bland-Altman LoA -58.06 ms (95% CI -59.34, -56.78) to 69.69 ms (68.41, 70.97), acceptance +/-99.5 ms. Endpoint 3 (AutoStrain with AI R-trigger vs ECG R-trigger): EF Pearson r = 0.892 (0.853, 0.922), GLS r = 0.992 (0.990, 0.994), acceptance LCB > 0.8; EF LoA -6.64% to 6.52%, GLS LoA -5.25% to 4.63%. Endpoint 2 (AutoMeasure, 32 parameters): all relative LoAs within acceptance bands, e.g. LVIDd -9.33% to 9.33% (criterion +/-30%), MV E Vel -12.00% to 12.98% (+/-25%), TAPSE -19.65% to 18.23% (+/-34%), RA Volume -27.08% to 32.89% (+/-46%). Stratified by race, region, cardiac health, age and BMI (Tables 6-7). Quote (p.15): 'The results of the 35 hypotheses demonstrated high agreement of R-trigger AI based algorithm in both technical and clinical assessments when compared to ECG -based R-trigger.'

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems

ai_features.name: Smart View Select (SVS) v2
ai_features.function: Deep-learning view classification of acquired adult TTE images plus a non-AI depth-based heuristic to automatically pick the optimal apical triplet (A4C, A2C, A3C) for launching AutoStrain LV or 2D Auto LV (EF/GLS) without manual clip selection. This K expands SVS to Affiniti and modifies it on EPIQ (revised neural network and revised depth heuristic, depth restriction 12-20 cm). SVS v1 on EPIQ was cleared under K240850.
ai_features.quote: This feature automatically classif ies each acquired image by view and selects an appropriate set of images for left ventricle (LV) analysis. The classification is based on a Deep Learning AI interface engine; the selection is a non-AI algorithm that considers the view classification and image depth to select the optimal set of images.

records.performance_summary: Retrospective study: three clinical experts manually selected apical clips and ran AutoStrain LV (average = ground truth); the same exams were processed by SVS with unedited AutoStrain LV output. Co-primary endpoints EF and GLS correlation, acceptance LCB of Pearson r > 0.8. Results: EF r = 0.891 (95% CI 0.851, 0.920); GLS r = 0.906 (95% CI 0.871, 0.931); criteria met (p.20: 'the Pearsons' correlation coefficient was 0.891 (95%CI 0.851, 0.920) for the EF and 0.906 (95%CI 0.871, 0.931) for the GLS measurement'). Bland-Altman performed but values not reported. Demographics available for a 71-patient US subset (53.5% male, age 61.0+/-16.4 y, 60.6% Black, 35.2% White, BMI 29.7+/-6.7; LV systolic function normal 64.8%, severe 15.5%). Total study N not stated.

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System

ai_features.name: Smart View Select (SVS) v2 Contrast
ai_features.function: Deep-learning (LVivo Seamless neural network) view classification revised to select the optimal contrast-enhanced A4C/A2C image pair (falling back to non-contrast images) from adult TTE exams for automated processing by 2D Auto EF Adv (contrast EF), and also feeds 2D Auto EF, AutoStrain LV and 2D Auto LV. User can override selected images.
ai_features.quote: The classification is based on a Deep Learning AI inference engine; the selection i s a non-AI algorithm that considers the view classification and image depth to select the optimal set of images. The difference in SVS v2 Contrast from the predicate SVS v1 (K240850) is that the algorithm is revised to include the selection of optimal images for analysis when contrast is used in routine TTE exams.

ai_features.name: 2D Auto EF Advanced (Contrast EF)
ai_features.function: AI-based contrast-enhanced biplane LVEF application (DiA LVivo, K243235; integrated on EPIQ/Affiniti under K251110) that consumes the SVS v2 Contrast-selected clips; referenced as the downstream application, not the subject of this K.
ai_features.quote: SVS v2 Contrast is an automated software feature that assists in the selection of images for analysis with the new Philips license options 2D Auto EF Advanced (Adv) developed by DiA Imaging Analysis (K243235), now part of Philips Ultrasound LLC

records.performance_summary: Retrospective sub-analysis of K240850/K243235 data on Philips-acquired contrast TTE exams: 60 subjects enrolled, 56 in sample, 46 evaluable (10 non-reportable); 62.3% male of 53 with sex data; age 20-87; US site mean age 63+/-15.8 y, BMI 31.9+/-8; 40.4% Black, 42.6% White, 4.3% Asian. Primary endpoint: biplane EF from SVS-selected clips vs Contrast EF on manually selected clips, acceptance LCB Pearson r > 0.8. Result r = 0.953 (95% CI 0.917, 0.974), p<0.0001; Bland-Altman mean difference 0.71 +/- 4.36 EF points (95% CI -0.58, 2.01), LoA -7.83 to 9.26. Versus manual tracing ground truth: r = 0.938 (0.890, 0.965), mean difference 1.22 +/- 5.22, LoA -9.01 to 11.45. Subgroups: male r 0.943, female 0.973, normal systolic function 0.926, abnormal 0.923. Quote (p.14): 'the Pearson's correlation coefficient and associated confidence intervals are 0.953 (95% CI 0.917, 0.974) for the Biplane EF measurement.'

records.device_name: EPIQ Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System; Affiniti Series Diagnostic Ultrasound System
records.exclusion_reason: Sole subject of the clearance is a Custom EMI Filter Module, an optional hardware spare part that filters powerline noise/poor grounding to reduce image artifacts; summary states it 'doesn't involve the software of the system' (p.10-11) and testing was EMC only (IEC 60601-1-2, 60601-2-37). No AI/ML feature is identifiable in the summary. Predicate is K250177 (Remote Software Management).

notes: Group philips-epiq-b, Philips EPIQ/Affiniti platform clearances 2024-12 through 2025-10, all read in full from the local FDA summary text files. Five of eight Ks carry a clearly named cardiac AI/ML feature: K243794 (AutoMeasure V3, ML-trained semi-automated adult TTE 2D/Doppler/M-mode measurements; 7127 clips/3964 subjects), K251110 (Auto EF with contrast, AI LVEF from contrast echo, r=0.952; plus SWM v2 ML segmental wall motion), K243793 (R-Trigger, AI R-wave detection from echo clips feeding AutoStrain/AutoMeasure; 7309 clips/3964 subjects, EF r=0.892, GLS r=0.992), K250886 (Smart View Select v2, deep-learning apical view classification for AutoStrain LV/2D Auto LV; EF r=0.891, GLS r=0.906) and K251455 (SVS v2 Contrast, deep-learning contrast view selection for 2D Auto EF Adv; n=46, EF r=0.953). Three are excluded: K242020 (Auto ElastQ, liver 2D-SWE frame/ROI recommendation; non-cardiac and not explicitly described as AI), K250177 (Remote Software Management, IT upgrade feature, no AI described) and K251651 (Custom EMI Filter hardware, no AI described). The K250177 -> K251651 predicate chain traces back to K242020 (Auto ElastQ), so the AI-list inclusion of those two Ks appears to reflect carried-over platform features rather than any AI content in their summaries. The common predicate for the cardiac-AI Ks is K240850 (EPIQ/Affiniti VM12/13 platform, which introduced SVS v1 and hosts AutoStrain LV and 2D Auto LV); Auto EF with contrast and SWM v2 were originally cleared as DiA LVivo applications (K243235, K243862). introduced_in_this_k is set true where the K introduces the feature or a revised version of it onto EPIQ/Affiniti (AutoMeasure V3 is a revision of AutoMeasure first cleared under K211597; SVS v2 revises SVS v1 from K240850); SWM v2 is marked false because the summary describes it as replacing the prior on-cart SWM with the already-cleared K243862 algorithm without modification. No web searches were needed; all decisions are grounded in the FDA summary text.
